title: Ordering events per order
description: An order service publishes created, paid and shipped events to a Kafka topic with 8 partitions. The fulfillment consumer group runs 8 consumers and must apply each order's events in order, but occasionally sees 'shipped' before 'paid'. Producers currently send records with no key. Throughput is fine. What is the right fix?

options.text: Reduce the topic to a single partition so all events are totally ordered
options.explanation: This gives ordering but caps the group at one consumer and throws away the throughput headroom; only per-order ordering is needed.

options.text: Add more consumers to the group so events are processed faster and arrive in order
options.explanation: Consumers beyond the partition count sit idle, and speed does not create ordering across partitions.

options.text: Produce each event with order_id as the record key so all events for an order go to the same partition
options.explanation: Kafka orders records within a partition; keying by order_id keeps each order's events together while different orders still spread across 8 partitions.

options.text: Have consumers sort events by producer wall-clock timestamp before applying them
options.explanation: Events for one order are spread across consumers, so no single consumer can sort them, and wall clocks on different producers can disagree.
